source_name: KfW Entwicklungsbank — tenders for financial cooperation projects (Montenegro)
why_relevant: KfW is a recurring funder in Montenegro (e.g. HPP Perućica upgrade with KfW as buyer) and finances financial-sector credit lines via local banks; its procurement notices and the German-side consulting-management tenders reveal implementing partners. Financial-sector KfW notices for ME are sparse but should be monitored.

source_name: Central Bank of Montenegro (CBCG) — press releases on EU/World Bank-funded payment projects
why_relevant: CBCG is the beneficiary/implementing counterpart of the World Bank + EU SEPA and TIPS-clone work. Its bilingual press releases confirm project scope, partners (Banca d'Italia, EU Delegation, World Bank) and go-live timing — the domestic mirror of the supranational contract record.

source_name: Directorate for Public Procurement Policy (Uprava/Direktorat za politiku javnih nabavki) — 'EU tenderi' section
why_relevant: Montenegrin government channel that republishes EU-funded tender opportunities and links national procurement rules to IPA/EU procedures — a bridge between the domestic CEJN portal and supranational notices, and a pointer to which ministries act as IPA contracting bodies.

source_name: Ministry of Finance of Montenegro — EU funds / IPA page (gov.me/mif)
why_relevant: The Ministry of Finance manages IPA funds in indirect management: contract preparation, conclusion and monitoring. Its EU-funds pages identify the national contracting structures and programme documents behind financial-sector IPA operations, and point to sectoral operational programmes.

source_name: World Bank Documents & Reports — Montenegro financial-sector documents (PAD, FSAP, procurement plans)
why_relevant: Full-text repository holding the Project Appraisal Document for P509405 and older diagnostics (e.g. FSAP technical notes on Montenegro). PADs contain the procurement plan and technical architecture — the most specific pre-tender description of what will be bought.

source_name: Commercial tender aggregators covering Montenegro + IFI notices (javne-nabavke.com, eKapija tenderi)
why_relevant: Regional aggregators monitor CEJN plus additional channels including donor/IFI notices, and index them in Serbian/Montenegrin. Useful as a cross-check that no supranational notice with a ME beneficiary was missed, and for local-language phrasing of tender subjects.

source_name: IFC Disclosure Portal — Montenegro financial-institutions investments
why_relevant: IFC invests in Montenegrin banks and leasing/fintech companies; Summaries of Investment Information name the client institution, instrument and purpose (often digitalisation or SME lending platforms), revealing which banks have external capital earmarked for systems modernisation.

source_name: CBCG — Registar platnih institucija i njihovih agenata
why_relevant: Authoritative, legally mandated list of licensed payment institutions and their agents operating in Montenegro — the ground-truth roster of non-bank payments-native players (PSPs, money transfer, payment facilitators) and how it changes over time.

source_name: CBCG — Registar institucija za elektronski novac i njihovih agenata
why_relevant: Licensed e-money institutions (wallets, prepaid, e-money issuers) in ME — a distinct competitive layer from bank acquiring and a leading indicator of fintech entrants.

source_name: CBCG — Spisak platnih institucija i institucija za elektronski novac kojima je oduzeto odobrenje
why_relevant: Reveals exits and licence revocations — negative-space intelligence on which PSP/e-money players failed or withdrew from ME.

source_name: CBCG — Registar platnih sistema
why_relevant: Which payment systems are licensed/operated in ME (RTGS/RTS-X, DNS, TIPS-clone instant scheme) — defines the rails PSPs and processors must integrate with, i.e. the integration-work pipeline.

source_name: CBCG — Podaci o platnim uslugama i elektronskom novcu (payment services statistics)
why_relevant: Quarterly reported volumes on payment services, cards, terminals and e-money — sizes the acquiring/processing market and shows growth trends that PSP competitors are chasing.

source_name: Asseco SEE — group structure and investor communications
why_relevant: Confirms legal entities per country (incl. Payten Montenegro, Monri), segment reporting and acquisitions — the cleanest way to track the payments competitor's footprint and revenue mix in ME/SEE.

source_name: Monri Payments — products and merchant references
why_relevant: Regional gateway (Asseco/Payten group) explicitly active in BiH and Montenegro; publishes merchant partnerships (e.g. Glovo for BiH/ME) — a direct read on which ME merchants are being won and by whom.

source_name: Klix.ba report — Monri Payments and Glovo card-payment partnership for BiH and Montenegro
why_relevant: Concrete, dated example of a cross-border PSP win covering Montenegro — the kind of announcement that reveals merchant-side contracts otherwise invisible.

source_name: CorvusPay — merchant-facing product and FAQ pages
why_relevant: Regional card gateway competing for SEE web-shop integrations; FAQ pages explicitly describe the merchant/acquiring-bank split, useful for mapping which ME banks it can settle through.

source_name: AllSecure — regional payment gateway platform
why_relevant: Serbia-based gateway/processing platform marketing into the wider region; a plausible non-bank competitor for ME e-commerce acquiring and white-label gateway deals.

source_name: Hipotekarna banka — e-Commerce merchant acquiring pages
why_relevant: A local acquiring arm that publishes its internet-acquiring offer (test environment, 3DS, PCI DSS, 24/7 support) — direct evidence of a Montenegrin bank competing as an e-commerce acquirer and of the technical stack behind it.

source_name: CKB (OTP Group) — Cards and POS terminals, corporate acquiring
why_relevant: Largest ME POS acquiring network (self-reported 4,000+ terminals since 2002); its product, terms and general-conditions PDFs expose acquiring pricing, 3DS and card-scheme arrangements.

source_name: Erste Bank Crna Gora — POS / card acceptance for corporates
why_relevant: Another ME acquiring arm; comparing POS/e-commerce offers across ME banks reveals which processor/gateway each bank rides on and where a vendor could displace incumbents.

source_name: Addiko Bank Crna Gora — POS terminali
why_relevant: Completes the ME acquiring-bank set; smaller acquirers are the most likely to outsource processing to a third-party vendor, so their pages are leading indicators of processing contracts.

source_name: Mastercard Montenegro — Banke prihvatioci (acquiring banks list)
why_relevant: Scheme-published roster of which ME banks are licensed acquirers — a compact, authoritative pointer to the full acquiring competitive set, snowballable into each bank's merchant pages.

source_name: Softing d.o.o. (Podgorica) — eCommerce integracije
why_relevant: Local systems integrator that documents which ME payment gateways it integrates (e.g. Hipotekarna eCommerce gateway) — integrators reveal de-facto gateway market share and named merchant projects that PSPs do not publish.

source_name: ecommerce4all.me — Montenegro e-payment module (CEFTA/Chamber of Economy platform)
why_relevant: Semi-official guide (Chamber of Economy of Montenegro + CEFTA project) explaining ME online payment processing, acquirers and regulation, with downloadable guide PDFs — an excellent starting map of the local PSP ecosystem and terminology.

source_name: Novalnet — Montenegro country payments page
why_relevant: Example of an international PSP marketing cross-border acceptance into ME; such country pages enumerate locally relevant methods and signal foreign competitive pressure on local acquirers.

source_name: PaymentProviders.io — Montenegro country directory
why_relevant: Aggregator listing providers claiming ME coverage; thin but useful as a snowball seed to discover PSP names not surfaced by local search.

source_name: Slobodna Evropa / regional media — TIPS-clone instant payments rollout in ME and BiH
why_relevant: Documents the Bank of Italy / TIPS-clone Western Balkans arrangement and the all-11-banks ME go-live — the single largest recent payments-infrastructure change, which drives PSP and bank integration spend.
